record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: Does every language in P-TIME admit a deterministic algorithm using at most O((log n)^i) space for some fixed exponent i? That is, is P-TIME contained in DSPACE((log n)^i) for some i?

evidence.quote: 5. Is P-TIME ~ DSPACE ((logn) i) for some i?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P denote the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in time polynomial in the input length n. For a function f: ℕ → ℕ, let DSPACE(f(n)) denote the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine using at most O(f(n)) cells of work tape on inputs of length n. Define
    PolyL = ⋃_{i ≥ 1} DSPACE((log n)^i).
Determine whether P ⊆ PolyL; equivalently, decide whether for every language L ∈ P there exists a fixed integer i ≥ 1 and a deterministic Turing machine that decides L using at most O((log n)^i) space.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether P is contained in PolyL (polylogarithmic space) is a long-standing open problem in complexity theory. It is widely believed that P ⊄ PolyL, but no proof is known; in particular, P and PolyL are known to be incomparable in the sense that neither is known to contain the other, and separating them remains open.

status_evidence.title: Complexity Zoo: PolyL
status_evidence.snippet: PolyL is not known to be comparable with P; it is conjectured that neither contains the other.

status_evidence.title: Wikipedia: L (complexity)
status_evidence.snippet: It is unknown whether P is contained in PolyL or vice versa.
status_evidence.claim: Inclusion P ⊆ PolyL remains an open problem.
